clips.text_zh: 睇個yield curve啦。兩年、十年、三十年全部扯高。Term premium又返嚟。Fed cut完又unprice返晒。又係學費。🙏
clips.text_en_b1: Bonds—bonds—bonds—bonds. Watch the screen. Two-year, ten-year, thirty-year—up they go. Basis points going lunatic. Fed cuts, that was the trade. Price it in, now unprice it. Term premium is back. The bond market is pricing the whole curve higher again, and nobody on /biz/ knows where it stops.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ OP yelling at the bond screen as yields rip higher

signal.rationale: OP tone screams that yields are ripping higher and the Fed cut trade is unwinding—implicit short-bonds / long-yield view

clips.text_en_b2: Bonds, bonds, bonds—keeping your eyes glued to the yield curve is non-negotiable right now. The two-year, ten-year and thirty-year are all grinding higher, with basis points behaving like they've gone completely off the rails. The Fed cut narrative was the trade, everyone priced it in, and now the market is unpricing the entire move. Term premium is creeping back, and the bond market is pushing the whole curve up again—nobody on /biz/ has the faintest clue where it stops.
clips.text_en_c1: Bonds, again, of all the things. The yield curve is the only thing that actually matters right now: two-year, ten-year, thirty-year, every tenor climbing in concert. Basis points have gone genuinely berserk as term premium resurfaces with a vengeance, undoing every basis point the Fed cuts supposedly gifted us. The market has fully priced in the cuts and is now pricing them right back out, which is a fairly humiliating reminder of how tuition fees accumulate. /biz/, characteristically, has no coherent thesis about where the rout actually stops, and the smarter traders have stopped pretending otherwise.
clips.text_en_c2: Look at the yield curve, if you would. The two-year, the ten-year, the thirty-year—each one has been dragged higher in what can only be described as a synchronised rout across the entire complex. Basis points are behaving quite irrationally, and the term premium, long dormant, has reasserted itself with a vengeance. The Federal Reserve's cuts, which the market had so confidently priced in, are now being unpriced with comparable conviction, a textbook case of whipsaw positioning. What we are witnessing is the bond market repricing the whole curve upward, and, rather predictably, the denizens of /biz/ possess neither the analytical framework nor the intestinal fortitude to divine where, precisely, this move ultimately exhausts itself.

clips.text_zh: Doge廢咗個penny。US Mint明明係全美國最賺錢嘅政府部門，cut off your nose to spite your face。又一個nothing burger。wtf。
clips.text_en_b1: Getting rid of the penny was a stupid token effort by Doge to show progress. The US Mint is literally the only profitable branch of government, a cut-off-your-nose-to-spite-your-face change. /biz/ says it is emblematic of the hair-brained stunts and nothing-burgers coming out of this administration. Markets shrugged it off today.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ OP mocking the penny abolition as a Doge stunt

signal.rationale: OP is political mockery of Doge (the department), not a Dogecoin (the coin) trade setup

clips.text_en_b2: Scrapping the penny was the kind of half-baked token gesture Doge loves to trumpet as progress. The US Mint is genuinely the only profitable branch of the entire federal government, so gutting it is the textbook definition of cutting off your nose to spite your face. Plenty on /biz/ reckon it's emblematic of the hair-brained stunts and nothing-burger announcements rolling out of this administration. Markets, for their part, simply shrugged it off at the close.
clips.text_en_c1: Abolishing the penny was yet another performative gesture by Doge designed to generate headlines rather than genuine savings, and the irony borders on the absurd. The US Mint remains, by any reasonable accounting, the only self-funding agency in the federal government, which makes the whole exercise tantamount to cutting off your nose to spite your face. On /biz/ it is being read as emblematic of the administration's hair-brained stunts, a textbook nothing-burger whose announcement the markets shrugged off within minutes. The symbolism outweighs the substance, as usual.
clips.text_en_c2: Doge's abolition of the penny ought to be regarded as little more than a performative gesture, a token sacrifice designed to project fiscal rectitude without actually delivering any. The United States Mint, lest we forget, remains the singular branch of the federal government that consistently generates revenue, which renders this particular intervention a textbook exercise in cutting off one's nose to spite one's face. On /biz/, the consensus is that the move epitomises the administration's predilection for hair-brained stunts and theatrical nothing-burgers, initiatives engineered for the cameras rather than for sound policymaking. Equity markets, characteristically indifferent to such frippery, responded with a collective shrug.

clips.text_zh: 睇完真係笑左。Canada跟歐盟玩法，no voting rights，austerity，再elect極端政府。Greece 2.0。HK樓市都係咁。🧐
clips.text_en_b1: Canada joins the EU associate club and literally has no voting rights while France and Germany strip what little economy it has left. The rest of Europe then austeritys it to death, Canada complains, elects an extremist government, and still cannot do anything because EU associate means no say. /pol/ calls it Greece 2.0.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ OP warning Canada is becoming another Greece under EU rule

signal.rationale: Macro rant, not an actionable trade

clips.text_en_b2: Reading through the whole saga is genuinely laughable—Canada effectively joins the EU associate club and discovers it has zero voting rights while France and Germany quietly strip away what little economic dignity it has left. The rest of Europe then proceeds to austerity it into the ground, Canada whinges about it, the electorate swings toward an extremist government, and still nothing changes because associate membership means precisely zero say. /pol/ is calling it Greece 2.0, and honestly, the parallels are hard to ignore.
clips.text_en_c1: Canada has formally entered the EU associate orbit, and the details, once you read past the spin, are genuinely farcical. Associate membership grants no voting rights whatsoever, while France and Germany proceed to hollow out whatever remains of Canadian industrial capacity. Austerity will follow, public discontent will metastasise, and an extremist government will duly be elected, only to discover that its hands are tied by the very arrangement it inherited. /pol/ is calling it Greece 2.0, and honestly, the analogy holds up uncomfortably well.
clips.text_en_c2: The spectacle of Canada acceding to associate membership in the European Union is, frankly, risible when one examines the terms with any rigour. Ottawa acquires precisely zero voting rights while France and Germany proceed to dismantle what remains of the Canadian economic base, extracting concessions through the sort of diplomatic choreography that Greece endured a decade ago. Austerity will be imposed, complaints will ensue, an extremist government will be duly elected, and yet Canada will remain structurally powerless, constrained by a framework in which consultation is offered but consent is never granted. /pol/ has already christened it Greece 2.0, and the comparison, however unflattering, is not entirely without merit.

clips.text_zh: Boston Dynamics似監倉，Tesla似Pepsiman。邊個整到好似貓女maid咁靚嘅AI robot出嚟？我課金。👍
clips.text_en_b1: Is any company actually working on domestic robots that look appealing, like aesthetically? China has uncanny AI Instagram-face bots, Boston Dynamics has claw dogs and bipedal cage-men, Tesla has Pepsiman bots, and Honda has the Awesomo. Nobody is making a cute maid or catgirl that runs around doing laundry without creeping people out.
clips.source_hint: /g/ OP asking why all home robots look cursed

signal.rationale: Cultural complaint about robot aesthetics, no trade setup

clips.text_en_b2: Is anybody actually developing domestic robots that look visually appealing rather than deeply unsettling? China is churning out uncanny Instagram-face bots, Boston Dynamics keeps rolling out claw-dogs and bipedal prison-inmates, Tesla is going full Pepsiman, and Honda gave us the Awesomo. Despite all that, not a single firm seems willing to ship a catgirl or a maid that runs around doing the laundry without creeping people out—somebody needs to crack that, because I'd happily throw money at it.
clips.text_en_c1: Is any firm genuinely pursuing domestic robotics that prioritises aesthetics alongside utility, or are we condemned to a future of uncanny contraptions? China churns out those unsettling Instagram-face bots, Boston Dynamics remains committed to claw-toothed quadrupeds and bipedal figures that resemble prison inmates, Tesla's Optimus looks like Pepsiman reimagined, and Honda's Asimo is a museum piece at best. Nobody, it seems, has the appetite to ship a catgirl-styled maid capable of folding laundry without inducing existential dread. Whoever cracks that brief first will, frankly, take my money without hesitation.
clips.text_en_c2: Is any firm genuinely attempting to produce domestic robots possessing genuine aesthetic appeal, as opposed to the dystopian bric-à-brac currently saturating the market? China has given us uncanny valley Instagram-face automata, while Boston Dynamics offers claw-footed quadrupeds and bipedal units that resemble escaped inmates. Tesla's Optimus evokes, somewhat inexplicably, the Japanese mascot Pepsiman, and Honda's abandoned Asimo remains the platonic ideal of endearing robotics. Nobody, it seems, has had the temerity to develop a fetching catgirl or a comely maid capable of performing laundry duties without inducing existential discomfort. Should such a contrivance materialise, my subscription shall be immediate and unconditional.

clips.text_zh: GPT-6 Astra勁到癲。zero-shot已經識control robot做物理task，配合π0.5喺RoboDojo贏晒。靠AI續命。btw，我份工幾時畀佢取代？😬
clips.text_en_b1: OpenAI's latest model, GPT-6 Astra, is insanely good at manipulating robots to do physical tasks and nobody on /g/ knows why. An anonymous Galaxy General evaluation report shows zero-shot generalization on the RoboDojo benchmark, and pairing Astra with the robot model π0.5 beat every prior setup. Nvidia's Jensen would call this made up.
clips.source_hint: /g/ OP hyped about GPT-6 Astra robotics results

signal.rationale: AI capability post, not a direct trade idea

clips.text_en_b2: GPT-6 Astra is, quite frankly, absurdly capable when it comes to steering robots through physical tasks, and nobody on /g/ has the foggiest idea why. A leaked Galaxy General evaluation report reportedly demonstrated near-perfect zero-shot generalization on the RoboDojo benchmark, while pairing Astra with the π0.5 robot model apparently demolished every prior setup. Jensen Huang over at Nvidia would probably dismiss the whole thing as fabricated. Meanwhile, half of /g/ is quietly wondering when their own job is getting taken.
clips.text_en_c1: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra is, by all accounts, genuinely unsettling in its proficiency at robotic manipulation, and the benchmarks only reinforce that impression. An anonymised Galaxy General evaluation report has surfaced demonstrating zero-shot generalisation on RoboDojo tasks, and when Astra is paired with the π0.5 control model, the combined system decisively outperforms every prior configuration. Nvidia's Jensen would presumably dismiss the figures as fabricated, but the empirical gap is now difficult to explain away. If this trajectory holds, my own role is on a fairly short runway.
clips.text_en_c2: OpenAI's freshly unveiled GPT-6 Astra demonstrates capabilities in robotic manipulation that border on the hallucinatory, at least according to the anonymous Galaxy General evaluation report circulating on /g/. Zero-shot generalisation on the RoboDojo benchmark is itself remarkable, but pairing Astra with the π0.5 robotic foundation model produced results that comprehensively outperformed every prior configuration, a feat that Jensen Huang would presumably attribute to hallucinations in the press release. The broader implication, that white-collar cognitive labour may be approaching its own inflection point, has not been lost on the readership, many of whom are now earnestly inquiring, with a measure of gallows humour, when their own positions shall be rendered superfluous.

clips.text_zh: 今日返gym做返deadlift。220kg兩下，PR 240kg。肥仔信你睇到未？我仲要再試245。💪
clips.text_en_b1: I went deadlifting again and pulled 220 kg for a double. I think I am just good at single reps, not higher reps. My previous PR was 240 kg and I have gotten stronger since, so next time I should try 245 or 250 kg. This was my first deadlift session in over a month, only kettlebell clean and press at home before this.
clips.source_hint: /fit/ OP posting a 220 kg deadlift double and chasing a new PR
clips.text_en_b2: Got back to the gym today and pulled 220 kg for a clean double on deadlift, which I'm quietly chuffed about. I've always reckoned I'm built for heavy singles rather than grinding out high-rep sets, and my previous PR sat at 240 kg, so next session I'll likely push for 245 or even 250. This was genuinely my first proper deadlift session in well over a month—just kettlebell cleans and overhead pressing at home before today.
clips.text_en_c1: Returned to the gym today after what felt like an eternity and finally put myself through a proper deadlift session, pulling 220 kilograms for a clean double. My single-rep ceiling has always felt like my stronger suit, although I suspect that is partly a function of conditioning rather than raw strength. My previous PR sat at 240, and given the strength gains I have clearly accumulated since, I should be aiming for 245 or even 250 next time out. Prior to today, my training had consisted entirely of kettlebell clean and press work at home.
clips.text_en_c2: I returned to the gym today after a hiatus of over a month, during which time the only meaningful resistance training I had undertaken consisted of kettlebell cleans and presses performed at home. The session's principal event was a deadlift of 220 kilograms for a double, executed with what I can only describe as adequate, if unspectacular, form. My previous personal record stands at 240 kilograms, and given the tangible gains in strength I have accrued through supplementary work, I intend to make an attempt at either 245 or 250 kilograms during the subsequent session, provided my central nervous system consents to cooperate. The trajectory remains upward.

clips.text_zh: Yuru Camp第四季春天出。等緊嗰陣不如每星期重溫兩集。Comfy到爆，睇完可以頂多一日OT。🧘
clips.text_en_b1: Gentlemen, we have decided to do a rewatch of Yuru Camp. In preparation for season four, which we anticipate will air in spring of next year, we shall watch one to two episodes per week of the first three seasons, plus the OVAs and the movie at the right time. It may be your first time or your tenth, fun will be had.
clips.source_hint: /a/ OP organizing a Yuru Camp rewatch ahead of S4
clips.text_en_b2: Right then, gentlemen, the long-overdue Yuru Camp rewatch is officially back on the table while we wait for season four to drop in spring. The plan is to chip away at one to two episodes a week across the first three seasons, with the OVAs and the movie slotted in at the appropriate moments down the line. Whether it's your first run-through or your tenth, the thing is relentlessly comfy—wholesome enough to soften the blow of another overtime shift.
clips.text_en_c1: Gentlemen, a proposal has been put before the council: a collective rewatch of Yuru Camp, timed to coincide with the impending release of season four in the spring. Between now and then, we shall convene weekly, working through one to two episodes of the first three seasons, with the OVAs and the theatrical film scheduled at the appropriate junctures. Whether this constitutes your inaugural viewing or your umpteenth, the consensus is unanimous that comfort of this calibre ought to be rationed responsibly, lest it lose its restorative potency after a particularly gruelling overtime shift.
clips.text_en_c2: Gentlemen, a proposition has been advanced, and after due deliberation we have elected to embark upon a communal rewatch of Yuru Camp in anticipation of the forthcoming fourth season, which we anticipate shall grace our screens sometime during the spring of the coming year. Our prescribed regimen consists of one to two episodes per week drawn from the initial three seasons, with the various OVAs and the theatrical film to be slotted in at the appropriate junctures. Whether this constitutes your inaugural viewing or your tenth, the consensus is that conviviality shall be the order of the day, and the resultant serenity ought to fortify us against an additional day of overtime, however reluctantly endured.
